reviews.body:
@pcbeingused333 thanks, this fixes the `KeyError` when `accelerator` isn't set, and `"auto"`, `"gpu"`, `"cpu"` and `CUDAAccelerator()` behave as before. I couldn't run a real Spark job (no Java runtime here), so I stubbed `TorchDistributor` and ran the captured training function locally. Changes requested, see the inline comments.

While you're here, `is_gpu_accelerator` doesn't treat `accelerator="cuda"`, which Lightning accepts as a GPU accelerator, as a GPU, so it gets `use_gpu=False` on any machine. Please add `"cuda"` to the check.

review_comments.body:
This only resolves the default on the driver. The workers still get `trainer_kwargs` without `accelerator`, so Lightning resolves `"auto"` again on each worker, and that can disagree with `use_gpu`. On an Apple-silicon machine in local mode it picks MPS and DDP fails ("strategies from the DDP family are not supported on the MPS accelerator"), while passing `accelerator="cpu"` trains fine. Please resolve it once and pass the result to the workers, e.g.

```python
use_gpu = is_gpu_accelerator(self.trainer_kwargs.get("accelerator", "auto"))
trainer_kwargs = {"accelerator": "gpu" if use_gpu else "cpu", **self.trainer_kwargs}
```

and send that `trainer_kwargs` to `distributor.run`, so the driver and the workers always agree.
Please move this into the existing `tests/test_distributed.py`, which already holds the `BaseModel` distributed tests.

This only covers a missing key, on a `SimpleNamespace` instead of a model. Please parametrize over the accelerator settings (missing, `"auto"`, `"cpu"`, `"gpu"`, `"cuda"`) with `CUDAAccelerator.is_available` patched both ways. Use a real model (e.g. `NHITS(h=7, input_size=14, max_steps=1)`) so the test goes through `__init__`'s CUDA default, and check the `accelerator` in the `trainer_kwargs` passed to `distributor.run`, so the driver and the workers are pinned to agree.

Since the `spark` extra provides pyspark, `monkeypatch.setattr("pyspark.ml.torch.distributor.TorchDistributor", Fake)` (with `pytest.importorskip("pyspark")`) is simpler than building fake modules in `sys.modules`.

Thanks for the review. Done in the new commit: when `accelerator` is missing or `"auto"`, `_fit_distributed` now resolves it once on the driver (`"gpu"`/`"cpu"`, same value that feeds `use_gpu`) and sends that `trainer_kwargs` to `distributor.run`, so the workers no longer re-resolve `"auto"` (e.g. to MPS). `"cuda"` is now treated as a GPU accelerator. The test moved into `tests/test_distributed.py` and is parametrized over missing, `"auto"`, `"cpu"`, `"gpu"`, `"cuda"` with `CUDAAccelerator.is_available` patched both ways, using a real `NHITS(h=7, input_size=14, max_steps=1)` and a fake `TorchDistributor` (`pytest.importorskip("pyspark")`) that records `use_gpu` and the `accelerator` in the `trainer_kwargs` passed to `run`.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
@alejandroxag , can you merge main and solve the conflicts please?

Merged current `main` into this branch as requested. The only conflict was in `_fit_distributed`: `main` now detects the accelerator through the shared `_is_gpu_accelerator` helper (which already covers `cuda`), so the branch uses that helper and keeps only the driver-side resolution of `"auto"` that is passed to the workers.

`tests/test_distributed.py` passes after the merge (14 passed); `test_fit_distributed_pins_accelerator` fails on `main` for the `"auto"` cases (workers receive `"auto"`) and passes on this branch. `ruff check` is clean on the touched files.

This followup was prepared with assistance from an AI coding agent.
